customer_demands: list[float]; required, one-dimensional array whose length defines the number of customers n; n=0 or n=1 is allowed. Array index k corresponds to customer id i=k+1; customer ids are fixed as 1 to n and the depot id is fixed as 0; all customer arrays use this order. Each entry is a finite positive real in the same quantity unit as vehicle_capacity; the unit name is unspecified. float always means a finite JSON number; integer notation is allowed, strings, NaN and infinities are not accepted. A single demand exceeding capacity is still a valid but infeasible instance, and that customer must not be removed.
vehicle_capacity: float; required, finite positive real, the capacity of each homogeneous vehicle, in the same quantity unit as customer_demands. All vehicles start empty; no fleet-size field is provided and no additional limit on the number of vehicles is imposed. When the sum of the demands of customers i and j exceeds this value, the customer arc i→j is forbidden in advance; equality does not forbid it. Even when n=0, this field must be positive.
customer_service_times: list[float]; required, one-dimensional array of length n; index k corresponds to customer k+1. Each entry is a finite non-negative real in the same time unit as the base travel times; zero is allowed, and it need not be an integer or an integer multiple of 0.1. The service time is added only to the outgoing effective travel time of the departing customer and is not added again at the destination customer or in any other timing step. [] when n=0.
customer_time_windows: list[list[float]]; required, shape [n][2]. First-axis index k corresponds to customer k+1; the second axis is fixed as [ready_time, due_time], the earliest and latest allowed departure times. Both entries are finite non-negative reals with ready_time<=due_time; no fixed time grid is required. All windows share the same absolute time axis and time unit, and both ends are inclusive. They constrain the customer departure time; no additional condition "departure time + service time must not exceed due_time" is imposed. Let a_i and b_i be these two endpoints for customer i; when a_i+c_ij>b_j, the customer arc i→j is forbidden in advance, where c_ij is computed as described for base_travel_times. [] when n=0.
depot_time_window: list[float]; required, length 2, fixed as [horizon_start, horizon_end], denoted [a_0,b_0]. Both entries are finite reals with a_0<=b_0; their sign and precision are not otherwise restricted, and they share the absolute time axis and time unit with the customer windows. Each route may independently choose a departure time within the interval and must return to the depot within this closed interval; travel times to and from the depot must both be counted. a_0 is also used in the effective travel time correction when the destination is the depot. Depot demand, service time and vehicle departure load are all fixed at zero, with no separate input fields.
depot_coordinates: list[float]; required, non-empty one-dimensional vector of finite real coordinates; components may be negative. Its length d is the coordinate dimension of the Euclidean space of this instance, not fixed to two or three; components are given in the fixed order of the coordinate axes of that space, and the axes have no additional business meaning. Uses the same distance unit as the base distances; the unit name is unspecified. Only the depot coordinates already present in the problem are required; there is no new requirement to provide customer coordinates separately; travel data between locations use base_travel_times.
base_travel_times: list[list[float]]; required, full square matrix of shape [n+1][n+1]. The first axis is the origin location id i and the second axis is the destination location id j; id 0 is the depot and ids 1 to n correspond to the customer arrays. For i!=j, the element tau_ij is a finite non-negative number equal to floor(10*distance_ij)/10 of the distance between the two locations in the same Euclidean space; it must be an integer multiple of 0.1 and tau_ij=tau_ji; this is truncation, not rounding. The vehicle speed is 1 and the unit system makes base distance and travel time values interchangeable; no speed factor may be applied. The main diagonal is filled with 0 as a format placeholder only, and self-loops cannot be used; zero travel time between distinct locations is allowed. The matrix does not yet include service time or time-window corrections. For customer i and any distinct destination j (including the depot), take s_i, b_i and a_j from the other inputs and compute c_ij=max(tau_ij+s_i,a_j-b_i); when j=0, a_j is depot_time_window[0]. For arcs leaving the depot, c_0j=tau_0j. Effective travel times are not truncated again and may be asymmetric, and the input must guarantee c_ij<=c_ih+c_hj for pairwise distinct i,h,j; the truncated base matrix is not separately required to satisfy the triangle inequality. The Euclidean origin above and the effective-time triangle inequality are guarantees of valid input and must not be remedied by modifying the matrix. Customer arcs are also subject to the time-window and capacity pre-exclusion rules; no forbidden arcs or effective time matrix are input separately. When n=0 this field is [[0]].
